{{nihongo|'''Okadakuni Shrine'''|岡田国神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

The original deity of Okadakuni Shrine was Ikukunitama-no-Mikoto. Sugawara no Michizane has been enshrined since the Heian period, and until the Edo period this shrine was called Tenjingū or Kizu-eki Sōsha Tenjinsha.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it began in the ninth month of {{ill|Empress Kōgyoku|Q235296|qid=Q235296}} 5 ({{ill|659|Q31092|qid=Q31092}}), when Ikukunitama-no-Mikoto was enshrined. The first appearance in official history is an entry in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}} for the 27th day of the 1st month of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), recording the grant of the divine rank of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} to this shrine. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} it is listed as a major shrine.

In the Heian period, as {{ill|Tenjin faith|Q66890725|qid=Q66890725}} spread, Sugawara no Michizane (Tenjin) was jointly enshrined here, and from then on the shrine came to be called Tenjingū. In {{ill|Tengyō|Q1327340|qid=Q1327340}} 1 (938), in the 11th month, the co-enshrined Hachimangū was founded.

In May of Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was ranked as a gōsha. In March of Meiji 11 ({{ill|1878|Q7776|qid=Q7776}}), the government officially identified this shrine as the shikinaisha Okadakuni Shrine, and it was renamed Okadakuni Shrine. Regarding the identity of Okadakuni Shrine, Kasuga Shrine, a sub-shrine in the precincts of Katsute Shrine (Ōno, Kamo-chō, Kizugawa City), is also treated as a candidate shrine.

In 1983 (Shōwa 58), part of the 40,000-tsubo precinct land was sold to the Japan Housing Corporation, and the proceeds were used to build new shrine buildings. In 1988 (Shōwa 63), the old shrine building set was registered as a Kyoto Prefecture cultural property.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Kyoto Prefecture Registered Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible cultural property
** Okadakuni Shrine, 6 buildings (architecture) - registered April 15, 1988 (Shōwa 63).
*** 2 honden buildings - Edo period.
*** 1 haiden building - Edo period.
*** 1 stage building - Edo period.
*** 2 south/north parishioners' offices - Meiji period.
** Okadakuni Shrine documents, 76 items (plus one document box) (old documents) - owned by a private individual. Designated March 29, 2024 (Reiwa 6)<ref>{{PDFlink|[https://www.pref.kyoto.jp/kouhou/documents/kouho_498_0.pdf Kyoto Prefectural Gazette, March 29, 2024]}} Kyoto Prefectural Board of Education Notice No. 2.</ref>.

=== Kyoto Prefecture Provisional Registered Cultural Properties ===
* Tangible cultural property
** Okadakuni Shrine Sessha Ebisu Shrine honden (architecture) - registered September 29, 2017 (Heisei 29).
** Okadakuni Shrine Daihannyakyō, 514 items (plus 6 scripture chests) (old documents) - registered March 24, 2023 (Reiwa 5).

=== Access ===
* About 15 minutes on foot from Kizu Station
* Community bus: get off at Kawarada stop, about 8 minutes on foot
* Parking available before the overpass on the approach road
